privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: ONE was designed with "privacy by design" in mind: the vast majority of operations — merging, compressing, converting, editing PDFs, images, audio or video — run entirely inside your browser, on your own device. Your files are never sent to a server. This policy explains precisely what data is nonetheless processed, why, and what your rights are.

sections.heading: 1. Data controller
sections.body: The data controller within the meaning of the GDPR is [TO BE COMPLETED — official name of the publisher (full name, or company name + legal form + registration number)], reachable at [TO BE COMPLETED — dedicated contact email address, e.g. contact@yourdomain.com]. See the Legal Notice for the publisher’s full identification.

sections.heading: 2. Core principle: your files stay with you
sections.body:
The document, image, audio and video tools offered by ONE run exclusively on the client side, using browser technologies (WebAssembly, Web Workers, File API). Specifically:
- The file you import is never uploaded to a publisher server.
- No copy of your file, or of its content, is retained by the publisher, in any form whatsoever.
- Processing (merging, compression, OCR, conversion, etc.) happens in memory, inside your browser tab, and the result is offered for download directly from your device.

This local-processing approach is core to how the Service works and is not a switchable option.

sections.heading: 3. Data we actually collect
sections.body:
In line with the data minimisation principle (Art. 5.1.c GDPR), we only collect what is strictly necessary for the Service to work:
- Data stored locally in your browser (localStorage), which never leaves your device: theme preference (light/dark), chosen language, touch vibration and sound settings, history of the last 20 operations (tool name, file name, timestamp — never the file content), and your choice regarding the cookie banner.
- Technical connection data collected as standard by our host (Vercel) to provide the Service and secure its infrastructure: IP address, browser type, pages viewed, request timestamps. These server logs are managed by the host under its own policy and are not used by the publisher for commercial purposes.
- If you create an account (optional feature): your name, email address, unique account identifier, creation date and, if you sign in with Google, Apple, Microsoft, GitHub or Facebook, the profile photo and identifier sent by that provider. This data is managed by our authentication provider, Firebase Authentication (Google), so that you can find your account on all your devices. If you choose email and a password, the password is never stored in clear text: Firebase only keeps a secure hash. We never receive the password of your Google, Apple, Microsoft, GitHub or Facebook accounts.

The files you process are never part of this data: they never leave your device, whether you are signed in or not. We do not collect or infer any sensitive data or precise location data, and we do not use any third-party audience analytics (no Google Analytics or equivalent) or targeted advertising as of the date of this policy.

sections.heading: 4. Purposes of processing
5. Legal basis for processing
6. Recipients of data
7. Transfers outside your country of residence
sections.body: Our host (Vercel) and our authentication provider (Google Firebase) operate global infrastructures that may involve processing technical connection logs and account data in the United States or other countries where they have servers. Insofar as this concerns personal data of EU residents, these transfers rely on the appropriate safeguards provided by the GDPR (standard contractual clauses or an equivalent mechanism recognised by the European Commission, including the EU–US Data Privacy Framework where the provider participates). Your files themselves are never transferred since they are never sent to a server.

sections.heading: 8. Retention period
sections.body: The files you process are never kept: they exist only in memory while being processed in your browser and are erased when the tab or browser is closed. Preference data and the local history stay on your device until you delete them yourself (Settings page, “Clear history” button) or clear your browser data; the local history is also automatically limited to the 20 most recent operations. Account data is kept for as long as your account exists; you can request its deletion at any time (see “Your rights”), after which it is erased from Firebase Authentication. The host’s technical connection logs are kept for Vercel’s standard period for operating and securing its infrastructure.

sections.heading: 9. Data security
sections.body: The architectural choice of 100% local processing inherently reduces your data’s exposure: since no file is ever sent to a server, there is no database containing your documents that could be breached or leaked. The Service is also served exclusively over HTTPS (encrypted transport). Local storage (localStorage) remains subject to your own browser’s and device’s security mechanisms: we recommend keeping your browser up to date and securing physical access to your device.

sections.heading: 10. Your rights
11. Minors
sections.body: The Service is not specifically directed at minors and does not knowingly target children for data collection. If you believe a minor has provided us with personal data without the required consent, please contact us so we can delete it.

sections.heading: 12. Cookies and similar technologies
sections.body: Details of the cookies and local storage used by the Service, and how to manage your preferences, are covered in a dedicated Cookie Policy.

sections.heading: 13. Changes to this policy
sections.body: This policy may be updated to reflect changes to the Service (for example, the addition of a user account or a feature involving server-side processing). Any material change will be flagged on this page, with the "last updated" date below revised accordingly.

sections.heading: 14. Contact
sections.body: For any question about this privacy policy, or to exercise your rights, contact us at [TO BE COMPLETED — dedicated contact email address, e.g. contact@yourdomain.com].

cookiePolicy.title: Cookie Policy
cookiePolicy.intro: This policy explains what cookies and local-storage technologies are, which ones ONE uses, why, and how you can manage them. It complements our Privacy Policy.

sections.heading: 1. What are cookies and local storage?
sections.body: A "cookie" is a small text file placed by a website on your device. "Local storage" (localStorage) is a similar, more modern technology that lets a website store information directly in your browser, with no automatic expiry date. ONE does not use classic tracking cookies but relies on browser local storage, which is subject to the same regulatory framework (ePrivacy Directive / GDPR).

sections.heading: 2. What we do not use
3. What is stored locally on your device
sections.body:
The only items stored in your browser’s local storage are:
- one-theme — remembers your light/dark display preference. Strictly necessary for the interface to work as expected; no consent required.
- one-language — remembers the language you chose. Strictly necessary; no consent required.
- one-feedback — remembers your touch vibration and sound settings. Strictly necessary to respect your choice; no consent required.
- one-history — remembers the history of your last 20 operations (tool name, file name, date), for the convenience of the “History” feature you requested. Functional, enabled by default as it is a service explicitly requested by the user; you can clear it at any time from Settings.
- one-cookie-consent — remembers the choice you made in the consent banner, so it is not shown again on every visit.
- Account session (only if you sign in) — Firebase Authentication stores in the browser (IndexedDB “firebaseLocalStorageDb”) what is needed to keep you signed in, and ONE keeps a preview of your profile (one-auth-cache) to show it without delay. Strictly necessary for the account service you requested; removed when you sign out.

When you use a “Continue with…” button, a window from the chosen provider (Google, Apple, Microsoft, GitHub or Facebook) opens on its own site: that provider may set its own cookies there, under its policy, as with any sign-in to its service. None of these cookies are set on ONE’s domain or used by ONE for advertising.

sections.heading: 4. Legal basis and consent
sections.body: Items strictly necessary for the Service to work (theme, language) are exempt from prior consent under ePrivacy regulation. Local history, while not indispensable to displaying the Service, corresponds to a feature explicitly requested by the user when opening the History panel; we nonetheless collect your overall choice through the consent banner for the sake of transparency, and you can disable it at any time by clearing your history from Settings.

sections.heading: 5. How to manage your preferences
6. Retention period
sections.body: Local storage data has no automatic expiry: it stays on your device until you delete it manually or clear your browsing data. Local history is additionally auto-capped at the 20 most recent operations.

sections.heading: 7. Changes to this policy
sections.body: This cookie policy may be updated if the technologies used by the Service evolve (for example, the future addition of an audience-analytics tool). Any significant change will trigger a new consent request where applicable.
